jobs.title: Adjunct Clinical Faculty – ASN Program
jobs.description: Classification: Faculty / Part-time Description: The adjunct clinical faculty – ASN is responsible to the ASN program coordinator and the director of the Craigmiles School of Nursing. The position is part-time and does not offer benefits, as specified in the handbook. The part-time adjunct instructor in the HLGU-PN Program will assume a teaching assignment in the clinical setting. Education, Experience, and Training Minimum of Bachelor of Science degree in Nursing Current Missouri RN licensure (and Illinois if necessary) Current unencumbered Missouri RN licensure (and Illinois if necessary) is required Two to five years of clinical experience desired Duties include but are not limited to: Represent the biblical worldview, mission, vision, and core values of HLGU by one’s statements, teaching, and deportment Respectful of the history, heritage, and values of HLGU Represent HLGU well, both on and off campus Follow all HLGU institutional and instructional policies and procedures Clinical supervision of students in Nursing Courses Keep assigned students in their clinical settings Conduct pre and post-clinical conferences Evaluate students – prepare anecdotal notes, written evaluations and conduct evaluation sessions with students Attend nursing faculty meetings as scheduled Nursing Faculty Members must be able to meet the following physical requirements: Fine hand/eye coordination, oral communication, and written communication Sitting, standing, walking, bending, pushing/pulling, and climbing Exposure to blood and body fluids, exposure to hazardous chemicals, concentration on detail, and exposure to extreme heat, cold, and temp fluctuations Carry/Lift 1-50lbs* *Hannibal-LaGrange University does not require nor does it expect that an employee lift over 50lbs unassisted. Objects in excess of 50lbs should be lifted or moved with mechanical means or a team lift. Ideal Candidate: Hannibal-LaGrange University is proud to be affiliated with the Missouri Baptist Convention and faculty must be professing Christians, actively involved in the church of their choice, and have values consistent with Baptist Tradition. Appointment: Review of applications will begin immediately and will conclude when position is filled. How to Apply: Click here to apply. For any questions regarding the position, contact Human Resources at 573-629-3058, or via email at humanresources@hlg.edu. Hannibal-LaGrange University seeks to employ qualified individuals without regard to age, sex, race, color, national origin, or disability, who can function effectively within the college’s mission and purposes.

jobs.description: Apply CCPA - Associate Program Director & Open Rank Faculty San Luis Obispo, CA Apply Job Type Full-time Description A.T. Still University (ATSU) is a culturally rich environment leading the way in whole-person health education with cutting edge technology and instruction. From its inception in 1892, ATSU has had a long tradition of inclusion. The ATSU College for Healthy Communities is the newest College within ATSU located in the beautiful Central Coast region of California. The Central Coast Physician Assistant (CCPA) Program is the founding academic program within the College with the mission of educating culturally-humble physician assistants (PAs) from diverse backgrounds to serve the primary care needs of medically underserved communities. The Associate Program Director and open rank faculty of Physician Assistant Studies will report directly to the CCPA Department Chair / Program Director. The individual will be responsible to support the Program Director in leading and managing all aspects of the didactic and clinical phases of the PA Program and in leading a dedicated team of faculty and staff, and to teach courses, engage in service, and conduct scholarship.The responsibilities of the Associate Program Director and open rank faculty of Physician Assistant Studies will include, but will not necessarily be limited to, the following:Collaborate as a member of the programmatic leadership team, consisting of the Department Chair / Program Director, Associate Program Director, Director of Didactic Education, Director of Clinical Education, and Medical Director to achieve a shared vision for becoming recognized as the principal source of PAs from historically underrepresented groups providing culturally humble care to medically underserved communities.Provide leadership and oversight to the program’s holistic student admissions process.Oversee a student-centered process to manage academic progression, retention, and completion strategies.Serve as the primary on-campus point of contact for day-to-day program operations, providing leadership and support to didactic students and on-campus faculty and staffEnforce program and university policy among on-campus faculty, staff, and students and resolve time-sensitive student concerns requiring an immediate responseProvide on-campus support and mentoring through development and implementation of a new faculty onboarding program and a comprehensive faculty development program.Engage in the community to promote the PA profession, the College, and the University, and to help address critical primary care workforce issues on the Central Coast.Provide leadership for a robust community engagement program for students, faculty, and staff, including local student-driven activities that build student-faculty relationships and support an effective transition between the didactic and clinical year.Support the Director of Clinical Education in maintaining relationships with clinical affiliates and preceptors, including occasional participation in clinical site visits.Serve as a principal faculty member to educate a student body selected for their commitment to the CCPA mission using a holistic admissions process.Support student readiness to achieve all programmatic benchmarks (e.g., PACKRAT and PANCE) through identification of and intervention with at-risk students, in collaboration with program leadership and faculty advisors.Provide leadership for ongoing compliance with ARC-PA accreditation standards and best practices in contemporary physician assistant and health professions education.Contribute to the preparation and writing of ARC-PA applications and self-studies, required reports, and other accreditation submissions, ensuring content is accurate, aligned with ARC-PA expectations, and supported through documented evidence.Develop and deliver academic courses as assigned.Conduct and disseminate scholarship.Serve on departmental, college, and university committees as assigned.Engage in community and professional service. Requirements The successful candidate will have the following qualifications, skills, and accomplishments:Prior academic experience commensurate with appointment at the rank of associate or full professor is preferred.Leadership experience in the design, development, and implementation of didactic and/or clinical education programs in medical education is preferred.Preference will be given to applicants who can clearly articulate how they would contribute to the program’s mission and vision.Prior experience in the successful recruitment, onboarding, and development of faculty to be high-quality academics (teaching, service, and scholarship) is preferred.Substantial previous clinical experience is preferred.Effective communication and collaboration skills are required.Skilled in working with a variety of different student learning styles and collaborating with faculty colleagues.Ability to perform duties autonomously with minimal supervision and maintain confidentiality.Licensure in, or eligibility for, licensure in California as a PA, nurse practitioner, or physician (MD/DO) is preferred.Current NCCPA or relevant board certification is preferred.Experience with ARC-PA or another health professions accreditor (e.g., CCNE, LCME, COCA) is preferredAbility to make data-informed decisions, strong attention to detail and organizational skills, and a track record of executing high-priority tasks with high quality and prior to established deadlines.Interested persons should complete the ATSU employment application online, which includes a letter of interest, curriculum vitae, and the names and contact information for three professional references.The salary range for this position at the assistant level is 114,400 - 143,000, at the associate level is 131,560 - 164,450, and at the professor level is 157,872 - 197,340.
